pins.definition: Of a person: having a lot to do and no free time.
Having a lot to do, or currently engaged in an activity; not free.
Having a lot of work or tasks to do; not free.

situation: A professional chef during the absolute peak of a dinner rush in a tight, compact kitchen.
subject: the sheer density of tasks
brief: A cross-section view of a tiny, intricate kitchen where a chef is captured in a flurry of activity: one hand flips a pan while the other garnishes a plate, a telephone is tucked under an ear, and order slips are papered across every available surface. The kitchen is packed to the ceiling with copper pots, steaming bowls, and utensils, illustrating a space so full of ongoing tasks there is no room left for anything else.
prompt: A cross-section view of a tiny, intricate kitchen where a chef is captured in a flurry of activity: one hand flips a pan while the other garnishes a plate, a telephone is tucked under an ear, and order slips are papered across every available surface. The kitchen is packed to the ceiling with copper pots, steaming bowls, and utensils, illustrating a space so full of ongoing tasks there is no room left for anything else. layered cut paper filling the whole frame, real depth between the layers, crisp cast shadows, visibly fibrous card and translucent tissue, raking side light. Never a box, a shadow-box or a picture frame around the scene — the paper IS the world, not an object sitting inside one. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
